subject: DONE s323c: an unqualified DYNAMIC glob name installed into main, not the package in effect
description:
FIXED s323c (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: p-glob-assign-dynamic + p-dynamic-typeglob).

`*{"NAME"} = …` with an UNQUALIFIED name hardcoded the package to "main".  Perl resolves an unqualified symbolic name in the package IN EFFECT.  perl's own File::Path does

    BEGIN { for (qw(VMS MacOS MSWin32 os2)) { *{"_IS_\U$_"} = $^O eq $_ ? sub(){1} : sub(){0} } }

so every one of those constants landed in main::, and the very next line of the same BEGIN block (`!(_IS_MSWIN32())`) died with "The function |File::Path|::pl-_IS_MSWIN32 is undefined" — the cause line on three `00-report-prereqs.t` files of the widened CPAN board.  Both the assign and the rvalue (`*{EXPR}` as a glob) now use `*pcl-current-package*`.

Verified: `use File::Path; make_path(...)` gets past the load and creates the tree (it used to die at load).  The main-package case (a dynamic install at file scope) is unchanged — probed.

FOLLOW-ON EXPOSED, filed as #192: `remove_tree` then dies in a VMS branch, because 8 call sites of those same constants emit the BAREWORD AS A STRING (`(p-if "_IS_VMS" …)`), and a non-empty string is TRUE.
